children: Viking Therapeutics (VKTX) climbed more than 35% in premarket trading Tuesday after new data suggested patients using its experimental obesity drug VK2735 were able to preserve much of their weight loss even after moving to less frequent dosing schedules.

The study evaluated patients who first completed a 21-week induction period on weekly injections. During that stage, participants lost about 16% to 19% of body weight, while the placebo group saw little change.

Researchers then shifted some patients to maintenance treatment. Those receiving injections every other week retained about 97% of their average weight reduction, while patients moved to monthly dosing maintained roughly 90% of prior weight loss. By comparison, participants on placebo preserved about 61%.
Viking also reported that patients treated with the 17.5-milligram weekly dose achieved approximately 22% placebo-adjusted weight loss across the full 33-week study.

The company said safety findings were generally consistent with prior studies, with a small number of participants discontinuing treatment because of adverse events. Viking plans to evaluate oral maintenance regimens of VK2735 in a future phase of the trial.

title: Viking Therapeutics Stock Soars After Obesity Drug Delivers 22% Weight Loss
